summary: Both sessions converge on essentially the same game: a low-poly Songkran walking race with 6 ordered checkpoints, 3 red slippery-puddle hazards, a calm elder water-pouring finale, and a live leaderboard for 4 players. The decisive differences are in spatial design and time handling. With guards divides the 10×10 m courtyard into four private 3.9×3.9 m cells (2×2 grid, 1 m gaps) with a compact loop per cell, keeping players fully separated and treating the trees as a pre-play measurement task. Before guards routes every player through one shared zigzag across the whole courtyard that bends around both real trees, which uses the venue more fully but creates crowding risk for four simultaneous players (a risk Before guards itself flags and never resolves), and it places unmeasured trees as precise coordinate exclusion zones. With guards also keeps the full 180-second session from the brief, while Before guards silently shortens the round to 150 seconds. Before guards's build brief is more concretely specified (exact metre coordinates), but those coordinates rest on guessed tree positions, undercutting their reliability.
why: The two designs are the same game at the concept level, so the verdict rests on execution safety and fidelity to the brief. With guards's 2×2 grid of private 3.9×3.9 m cells is the single most consequential difference: it physically prevents collisions between four simultaneous first-time VR players, whereas Before guards sends all four through one shared courtyard-wide zigzag, names the resulting jostling risk itself, and then never resolves it. With guards also keeps the brief's full 3-minute round (Before guards silently cuts it to 150 s while still claiming 3 minutes) and treats the unmeasured trees as a pre-play verification task instead of baking guessed coordinates into a load-bearing route. Before guards is genuinely better in two ways — its build brief is far more actionable (exact metre coordinates for every element) and its route makes richer, more memorable use of the real courtyard and trees — but its coordinates are partly built on unverified tree positions, and the unresolved four-player crowding issue is a real safety and throughput problem for a noon-time festival booth with VR newcomers. On balance With guards is the safer, more faithful, and more internally consistent plan; Before guards is the more vivid but riskier one.

differences.aspect: Session length vs. brief
differences.with_rag: Keeps the brief's 3-minute session: 180-second limit stated in the options step (mechanics), the prototype flow (0:00–3:00 with a 'round ends when time is up' beat at 3:00), and the build plan (timeLimit: 180).
differences.without_rag: Shortens the round to 150 seconds in the options step (mechanics: 'จำกัด 150 วินาที'), prototype (flow ends at 2:30, HUD 'เวลาที่เหลือจาก 150 วินาที'), and build plan (timeLimit: 150), while the players_fit text still claims 'รอบ 3 นาที' (3-minute rounds). The brief's session_minutes is 3, so the extra 30 s is presumably queue/turnover buffer, but this is never explained and contradicts its own 3-minute claim.
differences.evidence: Options step mechanics: With guards 'จำกัด 180 วินาที' vs Before guards 'จำกัด 150 วินาที'; prototype flow With guards runs to 3:00, Before guards to 2:30; build plan timeLimit 180 vs 150; Before guards players_fit 'รอบ 3 นาทีเหมาะกับครอบครัว' contradicts its own 150 s limit.

differences.aspect: Multiplayer spatial layout and player separation
differences.with_rag: Gives each of the 4 players a private 3.9×3.9 m cell in a measured 2×2 grid with 1 m gaps between cells (prototype decisions: 'แบ่งพื้นที่เป็น 2 x 2 ช่อง ช่องละ 3.9 x 3.9 เมตร เว้นระหว่างช่อง 1 เมตร'; build layout_brief repeats 'each player gets ONE 3.9 x 3.9 m cell, with 1 m between cells'). Players physically cannot collide.
differences.without_rag: All 4 players race on separate virtual copies of one shared zigzag route across the whole 10×10 m courtyard, with no cell division, no lane assignment, and no spawn offsets anywhere in the three steps. Before guards's own options-step risk admits 'ผู้เล่น 4 คนอาจเบียดกันหากเร่งเวลา จึงต้องเว้นทางและกำกับการเริ่มอย่างเคร่งครัด' (players may jostle if rushing; spacing and start control needed), but the prototype and build plan never implement any spacing or staggered start.
differences.evidence: With guards prototype decisions step: 2×2 grid, 3.9×3.9 m cells, 1 m gaps. Before guards options risks: crowding risk named; Before guards build layout_brief: 'Four players race simultaneously on separate copies with a live leaderboard' with no spatial separation scheme.

differences.aspect: Handling of the two real trees
differences.with_rag: Treats tree positions as unknown until measured: options risk and prototype decision require measuring both trees and checking all four cells in the editor before play; build brief says 'The two real trees are not yet measured: check all four cells in the editor before play and move any cell or route that a tree obstructs.'
differences.without_rag: Makes the trees load-bearing route features ('เส้นทางซิกแซกอ้อมต้นไม้ทั้งสองต้น', flow beats 'อ้อมต้นไม้ต้นแรก/ต้นที่สอง') and in the build brief assigns them precise coordinates '(4.0,4.2) and (6.0,6.2) as hard exclusion zones' while adding 'verify their measured positions before placement' — i.e., the exact route geometry is built on unverified guesses, and any real tree offset forces re-routing the shared path used by all four players.
differences.evidence: With guards build layout_brief: 'not yet measured: check all four cells in the editor before play'. Before guards build layout_brief: trees 'at approximately (4.0,4.2) and (6.0,6.2)... verify their measured positions before placement'; Before guards prototype flow 0:50/1:50 routes around tree one and tree two.

differences.aspect: Use of the venue and spectator staging
differences.with_rag: Compact loop inside a 3.9×3.9 m cell uses only a fraction of the 10×10 m courtyard; the trees are obstacles to avoid rather than part of the experience. Spectators stand outside the right edge and watch the final puddle dodge, blessing, and portal (build spectator_plan).
differences.without_rag: The zigzag route spans the full courtyard, bends around both real trees, and turns them into memorable course landmarks; spectators watch from the south edge with the final dodge, blessing point, and flower portal all facing them (build layout_brief: 'clearly visible to spectators standing outside the south edge'). Richer use of the real space and a more distinctive MR experience.
differences.evidence: With guards build layout_brief: 'Design this compact route for one cell, not the whole floor.' Before guards build layout_brief: coordinates span (1.0,8.2) to (8.4,4.0) with the route curving 'safely around a real tree' (key_art prompt) and spectator sightlines to the south.

differences.aspect: Build-plan specificity
differences.with_rag: Build brief describes the route qualitatively: a small clockwise loop with six named checkpoints in order, hazard placements described relative to checkpoints ('the first after the scented-water stop on the approach to the market...'), plus clearance rules (1.2 m bypass, 0.6 m from cell edge). No metric coordinates.
differences.without_rag: Build brief gives exact metre coordinates from the NW corner for spawn, all six checkpoints, the portal, and all three hazards ('spawn (1.0,8.2); CP1 ... at (1.8,5.2); ... hazards ... at approximately (2.2,6.2)...'), directly matching the prototype sketch's normalized coordinates scaled ×10. Much more directly actionable for a builder — though the tree coordinates in the same list are unverified.
differences.evidence: Before guards build layout_brief: full coordinate list; With guards build layout_brief: 'Use a small clockwise loop... Place three red slippery-puddle hazards: the first after the scented-water stop...' with no numbers.

differences.aspect: Internal consistency of hazard placement
differences.with_rag: Consistent: options list 3 hazards, prototype sketch has exactly 3 danger zones (market, canal bank, spectator-side), decisions and build brief repeat the same three placements in the same order.
differences.without_rag: Minor inconsistency: the build brief places the first hazard 'at approximately (2.2,6.2) before CP1', but CP1 is at (1.8,5.2) and spawn at (1.0,8.2), so (2.2,6.2) lies between spawn and CP1 — workable, but the prototype sketch labels it 'แอ่งน้ำลื่นจุดแรก' near the flower-street segment without the 'before CP1' claim; also the prototype flow at 0:50 ties the first puddle to the garland-arch beat (after CP2), which does not match the build brief's placement.
differences.evidence: Before guards prototype flow 0:50: 'อ้อมต้นไม้ต้นแรกไปซุ้มพวงมาลัย พร้อมก้าวออกจากแอ่งน้ำลื่นวงแดงจุดแรก' (first puddle on the way to the garland arch) vs Before guards build layout_brief: hazard 1 'at approximately (2.2,6.2) before CP1'. With guards shows the same 3 hazards in sketch, decisions, and build brief.

differences.aspect: Fit to brief: theme, respect, players, feelings
differences.with_rag: Songkran street race with blessing finale; explicitly no Buddha images or sacred spaces as step-on props; walk-only, 1.2 m bypasses, decor outside paths; targets sensation (festival colour) and fellowship (family cheering, live leaderboard); first-time-friendly (walk and touch, short signs, 20-second comprehension test question).
differences.without_rag: Essentially the same theme, respect rules (no Buddha images, no monks, calm blessing), walk-only pacing, colour readability tests under noon sun, and audience cheering. Both hit sensation and fellowship equally well.
differences.evidence: Both options steps: environment_fit and players_fit fields make near-identical promises (noon-readable colours, no sacred imagery, walk-only, tourist-friendly); both prototypes include a respectful 'รดน้ำ' ending and sun-legibility test questions.

differences.aspect: Quality and honesty of the three-option set
differences.with_rag: Three clearly differentiated options (route runner, chess-piece tactics, sword-wave battle) with per-option scores, risks, and a justified recommendation; the battle option honestly notes its weaker fit to a temple setting ('โทนต่อสู้ด้วยดาบห่างจากประเพณีสงกรานต์ที่อ่อนโยน').
differences.without_rag: Same three genres with comparable scoring and risk notes; the tactics option honestly flags tree-dependence ('ต้นไม้สองต้นอาจบังพื้นที่จนจัดกระดาน 6×8 ให้ปลอดภัยยาก'). Quality of the option sets is comparable.
differences.evidence: Both options steps contain runner/tactics/battle entries with scores, scores_why, risks, and recommend=0 with rationale.

differences.aspect: Equipment/real-water safety
differences.with_rag: States all water is virtual, the route must be dry, and players must be separated from real splashing water (options environment_fit; build brief 'players must remain separated from real splashing water').
differences.without_rag: Adds the explicit hardware reason: 'ชุด VR ไม่กันน้ำ ต้องมีพื้นที่แห้งแยกจากการเล่นน้ำจริง' (VR headsets are not waterproof; a dry zone separated from real water play is required) in the options risks, repeated as 'the booth isolated from real splashing water' in the build brief.
differences.evidence: Before guards options risks: 'งานสงกรานต์กลางแจ้งเสี่ยงน้ำสาดและพื้นลื่น ชุด VR ไม่กันน้ำ'; With guards options environment_fit: 'น้ำทั้งหมดเป็นเสมือนและเส้นทางต้องแห้ง'.

with_rag_weaknesses: The compact 3.9×3.9 m cell loop uses only a small fraction of the 10×10 m courtyard; the two real trees are reduced to obstacles to check rather than features of the experience, making the MR design less distinctive than Before guards's tree-weaving route.

The build brief is qualitative — no metric coordinates for checkpoints or hazards — so a builder must derive geometry from the normalized sketch and prose descriptions, which is less directly actionable than Before guards's coordinate list.
Hazard and checkpoint placement inside the cell is described only relative to landmarks ('after the scented-water stop'), leaving more layout ambiguity at build time.
Spectator value is narrower: only the final puddle, blessing, and portal are staged for the audience, while most of the loop happens inside a small cell.
without_rag_weaknesses: Four players share one courtyard-wide zigzag route with no cell division, lane assignment, or staggered start; the session's own options step flags jostling risk but the prototype and build plan never resolve it — a real collision risk for VR-first-timers.
The round is silently shortened to 150 s against the brief's 3-minute session, and the options text still claims '3-minute rounds', an unexplained internal contradiction.

The build brief assigns precise coordinates to the two real trees while admitting they are unverified; the whole shared route geometry depends on those guesses, so any measurement error forces re-routing for all four players.
Hazard placement is inconsistent between steps: the prototype flow puts the first puddle on the way to the garland arch (~0:50), while the build brief places it before checkpoint 1.

The shared route crosses the entire courtyard, which also means each player's path passes near both trees and all hazard zones — more floor area to keep dry, clear, and supervised at a crowded festival.
improvements: For With guards: add metric coordinates (or a per-cell coordinate system) to the build brief so the route is as directly buildable as Before guards's, and consider letting each cell's loop acknowledge the trees visually even if it cannot route around them.

For Before guards: resolve the four-player crowding problem explicitly — e.g., staggered starts, quadrant lanes, or adopting a cell grid like With guards — before build, since the risk was identified but never addressed.

For Before guards: align the round length with the brief (180 s) or state explicitly that 150 s of play plus 30 s of transition fills the 3-minute session, and fix the contradiction with the '3-minute rounds' claim.
For Before guards: do not publish exact tree coordinates as placement targets before measurement; mark them as placeholders and make the route tolerant to measured offsets.

For both: specify headset sun/heat management and queue throughput for a noon outdoor festival (neither session addresses equipment heat or per-hour player capacity), and state how the live leaderboard is shown to spectators (screen vs. MC).

summary: Both sessions honestly convert the unsupported "shooting zombies" brief into a walking-only MR runner for the same 2.2 × 2.5 m bedroom, with the same checkpoint/hazard/portal machinery, the same scoring (100/checkpoint, −25 hazard, 300 finish), and consistent safety framing (no running, no jumpscares, bed kept clear). The key difference is which option was recommended and built: With guards recommends its safest out-and-back escape with a single hazard, while Before guards recommends its most challenging zigzag dodge with two hazards. Before guards fits the creator's stated feelings (challenge + sensation) and experienced-VR profile better and delivers a markedly more specific build plan; With guards is meaningfully safer in the tiny room and has a slightly more coherent story and a more realistic 5-minute pacing.
why: The creator is a 30-year-old regular VR player who explicitly asked for challenge and sensation, and Before guards's recommended-and-built game is the one that actually delivers those feelings through a learnable dodge skill, while still encoding walking-only rules, bed-aware hazard placement, and a test question verifying safe detours. Before guards's build plan is also substantially more buildable as written: exact hazard placement logic, spawn size, object budget, hex palette, and sightline requirements versus With guards's single looser paragraph. With guards's advantages are real — one hazard is objectively safer in a 2.2 × 2.5 m room, its pacing fills the 5 minutes more naturally, and its story chain is tighter — but its chosen design is the more conservative option that its own scoring ranked lower on fun and player fit, making it a weaker answer to this particular brief. The verdict is medium confidence because the safety trade-off in a very small room is genuine: for a more risk-averse creator, With guards would be the better call.

differences.aspect: Fit to the brief's requested feelings (challenge + sensation)
differences.with_rag: With guards recommends Option 1 'หนีซอมบี้ออกจากห้องนิรภัย' (Escape the safe room), an out-and-back route with only one hazard, and in the options step explicitly scores its own two-hazard zigzag option higher on fun (5) and players_fit (5) but recommends against it because of space risk. The chosen design's tension comes mostly from the 300-second timer.
differences.without_rag: Before guards recommends Option 3 'หลบมือซอมบี้ถึงวัคซีน' (Dodge the zombie hands to the vaccine), whose whole pitch is skill-based dodging: 'อ่านพื้น หลบมือซอมบี้ และไปให้ถึงวัคซีนก่อนหมดเวลา' (read the floor, dodge zombie hands, reach the vaccine before time runs out). Its options-step scores_why says it 'ตอบทั้ง challenge และ sensation' (answers both challenge and sensation) for an experienced VR player.
differences.evidence: Options step: With guards recommend:0 with recommend_why citing safety; Before guards recommend:2 with recommend_why 'ให้ทั้งความท้าทายและความลุ้นระทึกใกล้กับเกมซอมบี้ที่ต้องการมากที่สุด' (gives the most challenge and thrill closest to the wanted zombie game).

differences.aspect: Safety in the real space (2.2 × 2.5 m room, bed against wall)
differences.with_rag: With guards's built game has exactly one red contamination pool (0.35 m radius) placed on the return leg, and the prototype flow says the player 'อ้อมแอ่งเชื้อวงแดงหนึ่งจุดโดยไม่ต้องรีบวิ่ง' (walks around one red pool without needing to hurry). The options step scored this option's mr_fit 4 vs 3 for the zigzag, citing that two hazards 'กินพื้นที่ปลอดภัยมาก' (eat up much of the safe space).
differences.without_rag: Before guards builds two zombie-hand hazards into a zigzag in the same tiny room. It mitigates with explicit rules ('เดินเท่านั้น ห้ามวิ่งหรือกระโดด และระวังเตียงกับผนังจริงตลอดเวลา' — walk only, no running/jumping, mind the real bed and walls), hazard placement between checkpoints with a readable detour, and test question 3 checking the player can detour without stepping toward the bed. But two dodge moments inherently invite wider sidesteps near the bed.
differences.evidence: Prototype plans: With guards sketch has one danger zone (r 0.12); Before guards sketch has two danger zones (r 0.11 each) plus an 11-point zigzag path. Before guards's own options-step risk admits 'วงอันตรายในห้องเล็กอาจทำให้ผู้เล่นก้าวหลบกว้าง' (hazards in a small room may make the player dodge widely).

differences.aspect: Specificity and actionability of the final build plan
differences.with_rag: With guards's layout_brief is one paragraph: 4 named checkpoints with rough relative positions ('near the spawn side', 'at the far end'), one hazard 'on the return leg', 2–4 vignettes, palette names but no hex codes in the brief, and no object-count budget.
differences.without_rag: Before guards's layout_brief is far more operational: exact checkpoint order with per-checkpoint vignettes, a 0.6 m spawn circle, checkpoint spacing 0.5–1 m, exactly two hazards with scripted placement logic ('Put the first between checkpoints 1 and 2 so it blocks the direct line and teaches the player to stop, read the floor, and walk around it'), an object budget of 'roughly 8–20 small low-poly objects', hex palette (#171B2E, #38465A, #E34850, #72E0B8, #D9E4DD), and explicit sightline requirements from spawn.
differences.evidence: Build-plan step: compare the two layout_brief fields; Before guards also specifies 'Do not add any other hazards or enemies' and what the player should see from spawn, none of which appears in With guards's brief.

differences.aspect: Pacing realism and use of the 5-minute session
differences.with_rag: With guards's prototype flow spreads beats across the full session: checkpoints at 0:20, 1:10, 2:10, 3:10, hazard dodge at 3:45, score review at 4:30, ending at 5:00 — a believable walking pace with a wind-down.
differences.without_rag: Before guards's flow finishes all four checkpoints and the portal by 2:20, offers replay at 2:40, then has an idle 'หมดเวลารอบเล่น' (time runs out) entry at 5:00. For a 2.2 × 2.5 m room the ~2.5-minute completion is plausible, but it means the designed experience only fills half the session and leans on voluntary replay.
differences.evidence: Prototype-plan flow arrays: With guards last gameplay beat 4:30; Before guards last gameplay beat 2:40 with a padding entry at 5:00.

differences.aspect: Narrative coherence and theme
differences.with_rag: With guards's story beats form a logical chain — radio call → gather supplies → open the bunker door → send the rescue signal → escape portal — and the build-plan story ties them together ('ทางออกจะเปิดก็ต่อเมื่อเก็บเสบียงและส่งสัญญาณขอความช่วยเหลือครบถ้วน').
differences.without_rag: Before guards's chain (first aid → pass the car wreck → reach the vaccine cabinet → open the evacuation point) is serviceable but thinner; the wreck and first-aid stop are decorative rather than causal, and 'เปิดจุดอพยพ' (open the evacuation point) immediately followed by a portal is slightly redundant.
differences.evidence: Prototype storyboards and build-plan story fields in both sessions.

differences.aspect: Honesty about the missing shooting mechanic
differences.with_rag: With guards states in Option 1's pitch and prototype decisions that there is no gun because the engine doesn't support it ('ไม่มีการยิงหรือต่อสู้'), and its first test question checks the player understands within 20 seconds that they walk and tap, not shoot.
differences.without_rag: Before guards is equally explicit: Option 3's why says it 'บอกชัดว่าไม่มีปืนหรือการสู้' (clearly states no guns or fighting), the 0:00 flow card reiterates walking-only with no shooting, and the key-art prompt includes 'no guns, no combat'.
differences.evidence: Options pitches, prototype decisions, and key-art prompts in both sessions.

differences.aspect: Consistency between steps (options → prototype → build plan)
differences.with_rag: With guards carries Option 1 forward faithfully: same four checkpoint names, one 0.35 m hazard, 300-second limit, spooky lighting, and identical scoring in prototype decisions and build-plan rules.
differences.without_rag: Before guards also carries Option 3 forward faithfully: same checkpoint names, two hazards, scoring, and time limit; the build plan even adds a spawn-circle size consistent with the prototype sketch.
differences.evidence: Cross-check of mechanics fields (options), decisions/flow/sketch (prototype), and rules/layout_brief (build plan) in both sessions; no contradictions found in either.

differences.aspect: Replayability and skill depth
differences.with_rag: With guards's single hazard on the return leg offers little to master; replay value rests on time bonus only, and the prototype gives no replay beat.
differences.without_rag: Before guards explicitly designs for mastery: the end storyboard beat says 'เลือกเล่นซ้ำเพื่อลดเวลาหรือเลี่ยงการถูกหักคะแนน' (replay to lower time or avoid penalties), the 2:40 flow beat offers immediate restart, and test question 2 tracks which hazard catches players — treating the two dodges as a learnable skill.
differences.evidence: Prototype storyboard end beats, flow arrays, and test_questions in both sessions.

with_rag_weaknesses: Recommends its safest option over the one it scored highest on fun (5) and players_fit (5), so the built game under-serves the challenge half of the brief; tension relies mostly on the timer with only one dodge moment.

The final layout_brief is comparatively vague: checkpoint positions given only as relative hints, no object budget, no hex palette, no spawn specification, and no placement logic for the hazard beyond 'on the return leg'.
Limited replay hooks: a single hazard offers little mastery, and the prototype includes no replay beat or per-hazard failure tracking.
The out-and-back route reuses the same corridor, which Before guards's options step explicitly flags as a repetition risk for its own similar option ('การเดินย้อนเส้นเดิมอาจรู้สึกซ้ำ').
without_rag_weaknesses: Two dodge hazards in a 2.2 × 2.5 m room with a bed against the wall is the riskier configuration; its own options step warns players may sidestep widely, and safety depends on mitigations (walk-only rules, placement, testing) actually holding in the real room.
Pacing under-fills the 5-minute session: all content finishes by ~2:20–2:40 in the flow, leaving the 5:00 entry as a timeout fallback rather than designed content.
Story beats are more decorative than causal (first-aid stop and car wreck don't drive the escape), making the narrative thinner than With guards's radio→supplies→signal chain.
Checkpoint names and theme elements (vaccine, evacuation point, zombie hands) are somewhat generic zombie-kit compared with With guards's more specific bunker scenario.
improvements: Before guards should add an explicit minimum clearance spec between each hazard edge and the bed/walls (e.g., ≥0.5 m walkable detour lane) in the layout_brief, not just 'away from the bed', so the builder can verify safety numerically.
Before guards should either compress the timer to ~3 minutes or add a designed second phase (e.g., a faster return leg) so the 5-minute session is filled with content instead of ending at 2:40.
With guards should adopt Before guards's build-plan rigor: hex palette in the layout_brief, an object-count budget, spawn-circle size, and explicit hazard-placement logic tied to teaching the dodge.

With guards could recover some challenge without adding floor hazards — e.g., a second playthrough modifier (shorter timer, moved hazard) — to better serve the requested challenge feeling while keeping its safer single-hazard layout.

Both designs could address the original shooting fantasy more concretely within engine limits, e.g., a 'signal flare' or 'UV flashlight' tap-to-repel gesture at static zombies, which would feel closer to an action verb than pure walking while remaining buildable and safe.

summary: Both sessions converge on nearly the same game: a calm 5-stop loop walk through a nostalgic old Thai morning market for first-time senior VR users, ending near seated friends. The structures, safety metrics (1.2 m corridor, 0.6 m clearance), and option diversity are essentially equivalent. The decisive difference is pressure management: Before guards deliberately hides all scoring during play and states this consistently across its prototype decisions, HUD, and build brief, while With guards puts a large running score in the HUD and formalizes point values in the rules — a small but real contradiction of the brief's \"submission\"/no-pressure requirement and of its own pitch. Before guards also adds a seated desktop fallback for unsteady walkers and playtest questions that probe first-minute discomfort and balance, which matter for this exact audience.
why: Before guards is more faithful to the brief's core emotional requirement (calm, unhurried, nothing to fear) because it actively removes score pressure rather than adding it, and it is slightly stronger on real-space safety for unsteady seniors (explicit non-VR fallback, discomfort/balance test questions). With guards is not unsafe or off-brief overall — its layout engineering is equally rigorous — but its visible big-number score works against the very feeling the creator asked for, and its own pitch promised the opposite.

differences.aspect: Fit to the brief: requested feelings (submission, narrative) vs. scoring pressure
differences.with_rag: With guards's prototype HUD includes "คะแนนสะสมแบบตัวเลขใหญ่" (a big-number running score) and its decisions give 100 points per checkpoint plus 300 at the portal; the build-plan rules repeat the point values and the end storyboard beat has the player "ดูคะแนน" (look at the score) before removing the headset.
differences.without_rag: In the prototype plan, Before guards explicitly states that the system tracks points and time but does NOT display score during the walk "เพื่อไม่ให้รู้สึกถูกกดดัน" (so the player does not feel pressured), and its HUD list says "ไม่มีนาฬิกาจับเวลา ไม่มีคะแนน และไม่มีแถบชีวิตระหว่างเล่น" (no timer, no score, no health bar during play).
differences.evidence: Prototype step, hud and decisions arrays; build step, game.rules. The brief asks for "submission" (calm, unhurried) and the constraint "ปลอดภัยมาก ไม่ต้องรีบ" (very safe, no rushing).

differences.aspect: Internal consistency between steps (HUD vs. rules)
differences.with_rag: With guards's HUD shows a big running score during play, while its own option-1 pitch promises "ไม่มีอะไรให้รีบหรือกลัวพลาด" (nothing to rush or fear missing) and the brief asks for a pressure-free experience; the rules then formalize point values (100 per point, 300 at exit), deepening the mismatch with the promised mood.
differences.without_rag: Before guards's decision says scoring exists but is hidden during play, and its HUD list matches ("ไม่มีคะแนน ... ระหว่างเล่น"). The build-plan layout brief repeats "no in-play score or timer display", so the three steps agree.
differences.evidence: With guards prototype hud vs. option pitch; Before guards prototype decisions/hud vs. build layout_brief.

differences.aspect: Specificity of safety and layout engineering in the build plan
differences.with_rag: With guards's layout_brief likewise specifies a corridor at least 1.2 m wide, all virtual objects at least 0.6 m inside the play-area edge, no obstacles on the route, rest chairs outside the play area, and exactly 0 hazards.
differences.without_rag: Before guards's layout_brief specifies a walking corridor at least 1.2 m wide, all virtual scenery outside it, checkpoints and portal at least 0.6 m from the play-area boundary, spawn and finish close together on the south side, and staff beside spawn outside the route.
differences.evidence: Build step, layout_brief in both sessions. Both give concrete metric clearances suitable for a 6 x 6 m room with unsteady walkers.

differences.aspect: Accommodation for players with unsteady gait
differences.with_rag: With guards mentions rest chairs outside the play area and staff help, but offers no alternative play mode for participants who cannot safely walk the loop.
differences.without_rag: Before guards's prototype decisions include an explicit fallback: "เสนอทางเลือกเล่นบนคอมพิวเตอร์สำหรับผู้ที่เดินไม่มั่นคง" (offer a seated desktop-computer alternative for those who cannot walk steadily), and its option-1 risks repeat this.
differences.evidence: Before guards prototype decisions item 6 and option 1 risks; With guards prototype decisions item 6 (chairs only).

differences.aspect: Narrative climax and memory-sharing design
differences.with_rag: With guards's climax is the bench in front of the market ("ม้านั่งหน้าตลาด") inviting the player to recall a morning from the past, then exit near friends; the end beat is likewise "กลับมาพร้อมเรื่องเล่า".
differences.without_rag: Before guards's climax is the old-radio corner ("ฟังเสียงวิทยุเก่า") with no loud sounds or surprises, followed by the exit portal near friends; the storyboard end beat is "กลับมาพร้อมเรื่องเล่า" (return with a story to tell).
differences.evidence: Prototype step, storyboard climax/end beats in both. Both deliver a quiet reflective peak and a social debrief; radio vs. bench is a thematic preference, not a quality gap.

differences.aspect: Playtest questions targeting the real risks
differences.with_rag: With guards asks about sign readability, corridor stability, wayfinding for first-time headset users, and whether the stories prompt sharing — useful, but it has no question about discomfort, nausea, or balance incidents.
differences.without_rag: Before guards asks whether anyone requests to stop or feels unwell in the first minute, whether steps shorten, and whether anyone reaches for walls or staff for balance — direct early-warning checks for VR-first-time seniors.
differences.evidence: Prototype step, test_questions arrays. For 60–75-year-old first-time VR users, early discomfort detection is a primary safety instrument.

differences.aspect: Diversity and honesty of the three options
differences.with_rag: With guards offers the same three archetypes (walk, rook puzzle, sword defense) with the same low players_fit (2) for the battle option and the same caveat that it is not the main recommendation.
differences.without_rag: Before guards offers a market walk (runner/tour), a rook-movement puzzle (tactics), and a gentle sword game (battle), with the battle option explicitly scored low on players_fit (2) and flagged as conflicting with "ปลอดภัยมาก ไม่ต้องรีบ".
differences.evidence: Options step in both sessions: same genre spread, same scoring pattern, same recommendation of option 1.

differences.aspect: Checkpoint content and route clarity
differences.with_rag: Five ordered stops: open the market gate, grocery shop, fruit stand, old coffee shop, front-of-market bench; loop returning to start near spectators; stops 2–3 m apart.
differences.without_rag: Five ordered stops: greet the front-stall vendor, grocery shop, old coffee shop, fruit stand, old radio; loop with start and finish close together; stops 2–3 m apart.
differences.evidence: Options step mechanics and prototype sketch zones in both. Equivalent structure and spacing; only the flavor of the first and last stops differs.

with_rag_weaknesses: With guards shows a large running score during play and assigns point values (100 per checkpoint, 300 at exit), contradicting the brief's no-pressure "submission" feeling and its own pitch that there is nothing to rush or fear.
With guards offers no alternative for participants who cannot walk the loop steadily; only rest chairs outside the area are mentioned.
With guards's playtest questions omit any check for first-minute discomfort, nausea, or balance incidents — the main risks for first-time senior VR users.
With guards's end beat has the player look at their score before removing the headset, adding a small evaluative moment right at the emotional close that Before guards keeps purely social.
without_rag_weaknesses: Before guards still tracks points and time internally even though they are never shown; this is vestigial complexity that could leak into the UI during implementation.
Before guards's radio climax relies on audio nostalgia, which may land unevenly for players with hearing impairment, and no volume or subtitle accommodation is specified.
Before guards's story content is explicitly sign-only (acknowledged in its risks), so players who dislike reading get a thinner narrative.
improvements: With guards should remove the in-play score from the HUD (or hide it until after the exit portal) to match its own promise of a pressure-free walk and the brief's "submission" feeling.
With guards should add a seated/desktop fallback and a first-minute discomfort check to match the safety bar its own brief sets ("ปลอดภัยมาก").

Before guards should resolve the small residual tension of tracking time/points at all: if scores are never shown, consider dropping them from the rules to keep the build simpler and avoid any chance they surface in UI later.

Both designs could specify audio levels and a staff stop-signal (e.g., a spoken phrase or gesture that pauses the experience) since spectators are encouraged to cheer, which could startle an immersed first-time player.
Both designs could state a maximum walk distance per stop in meters within the 6 x 6 m loop to verify the 4-minute session against typical senior walking speeds.

summary: Both With guards and Before guards propose a neon sci-fi walking race through checkpoints with hazards, live leaderboard, and spectator viewing, fitting the brief well. However, With guards is superior in its concrete spatial planning: it assigns each of the 6 players their own bounded cell (5.9 x 6.27 m) arranged in a 2x3 grid with 1 m gaps, eliminating collision risk and making the MR implementation unambiguous. Before guards uses two long lanes spanning the full 22 m court for 6 players but does not resolve how players are physically separated, creating a safety and feasibility gap. With guards also provides more specific hazard placement (6 hazards with exact positions) and route detail. Both designs are consistent across steps and equivalent in spectator experience, game feel, and alternative option quality.
why: With guards is preferred because it solves the core MR safety and feasibility challenge of 6 simultaneous players in a shared physical space through a concrete cell-based layout (2x3 grid, 5.9 x 6.27 m per cell, 1 m gaps), while Before guards leaves this ambiguous with 'two long lanes' and 'six separated spawn positions' that do not add up for 6 players. With guards also provides more specific hazard placement and route geometry. Both are otherwise equivalent in brief fit, consistency, and spectator design.

differences.aspect: Fit to brief: running/race concept and play_mode
differences.with_rag: With guards's recommended option is a walking race through checkpoints with hazards, matching 'race through neon sci-fi course' and play_mode 'race'. It explicitly acknowledges the tension: 'the name and inspiration are running, but walking fast is safer in MR' (prototype decisions).
differences.without_rag: Before guards's recommended option is also a walking race through checkpoints with hazards, matching the brief. It also acknowledges the walking adaptation: 'adjusts the pace to safe fast walking in MR' (option 1 'why').
differences.evidence: Both options step 1 recommend a checkpoint race with hazards and leaderboard. Both convert 'running' to 'fast walking' for MR safety. Equivalent fit.

differences.aspect: Fit to brief: group size 6 simultaneous players
differences.with_rag: With guards assigns each of 6 players their own copy of the course in separate cells (2x3 grid, each 5.9 x 6.27 m), explicitly stating 'six separate cells arranged 2 x 3 with 1 m between cells' and 'each player walks in their own copy of the court' (build plan layout_brief).
differences.without_rag: Before guards also has 6 players each on their own copy of the route, but the layout uses 'two long, gently bending lanes spanning the full 22 m court' with 'six separated spawn positions' (build plan layout_brief). It does not specify how 6 players are physically separated in the shared court space.
differences.evidence: With guards step 3 layout_brief: 'six separate cells arranged 2 x 3 with 1 m between cells'. Before guards step 3 layout_brief: 'two long, gently bending lanes spanning the full 22 m court' and 'six separated spawn positions' — but no cell division or explanation of how 6 simultaneous players avoid interference on shared 22 m lanes.

differences.aspect: Safety in the real space: player separation and collision avoidance
differences.with_rag: With guards separates players into individual cells (5.9 x 6.27 m each) with 1 m gaps, keeps route elements 0.6 m from edges, preserves a 1.2 m walking route, and keeps four doors unobstructed. Test questions include 'six players enter their own starting cells correctly and do not cross paths during the race' (prototype).
differences.without_rag: Before guards uses two long lanes spanning the full 22 m court with six separated spawn positions, but the risks section admits 'players 6 still use the real space together, must separate starting positions and control not to cut lanes or run' (option 1 risks). The build plan says 'lanes must never cross' but does not explain how 6 players share 2 lanes safely.
differences.evidence: With guards step 1 option 1 environment_fit: 'six separate cells arranged 2 x 3'. Before guards step 1 option 1 risks: 'players 6 still use the real space together, must separate starting positions and control not to cut lanes or run' — acknowledging a safety concern that the cell-based approach in With guards eliminates by design.

differences.aspect: Safety: hazard placement and movement constraints
differences.with_rag: With guards places 6 hazards, all red energy-leak circles, with specific positions (H1-H6) and requires players to step out of red circles without running. Hazards are placed to maintain a 1.2 m clear walking route.
differences.without_rag: Before guards places hazards between checkpoints with increasing density, climax with two hazard groups on a narrow bridge, and explicitly states 'Avoid tasks requiring players to look up while moving' and 'retains the required 1.2 m safe corridor' (build plan layout_brief).
differences.evidence: Both designs specify hazard placement, safe corridor width (1.2 m), and no running. Before guards adds the 'no looking up while moving' constraint; With guards adds explicit hazard count (6) and positions. Equivalent safety rigor.

differences.aspect: Specificity: route and checkpoint detail
differences.with_rag: With guards specifies exactly 8 checkpoints with Thai labels in order, 6 hazards with positions (H1 after stop 1, H2 after stop 2, etc.), and a compact two-lane zigzag within a 5.9 x 6.27 m cell. The sketch shows a detailed path with 10 waypoints and 10 zones including specific hazard locations.
differences.without_rag: Before guards specifies exactly 9 checkpoints with Thai labels and approximate spacing (2.5-9 m apart), but the route is 'two long, gently bending lanes spanning the full 22 m court' with less granular detail on exact turns. The sketch shows a simpler path with 10 waypoints and 8 zones.
differences.evidence: With guards step 3 layout_brief: 'Use exactly 8 ordered checkpoints with these labels in order' and 'Place exactly 6 hazards... H1 after stop 1... H6 after stop 7'. Before guards step 3 layout_brief: 'Place exactly 9 ordered checkpoints, spaced approximately 2.5–9 m apart' — less precise on hazard positions and route geometry.

differences.aspect: Feasibility: space usage and MR implementation
differences.with_rag: With guards uses a compact cell-based approach (5.9 x 6.27 m per player) that fits within the 14 x 22 m court, explicitly calculating the 2x3 grid layout. This is highly feasible for MR as each player has a bounded, controlled space.
differences.without_rag: Before guards uses the full 22 m court length with two lanes, which is feasible for 2 players but ambiguous for 6 simultaneous players. The build plan mentions 'six separated spawn positions' but does not resolve how 6 players share 2 lanes without interference or how the space is divided.
differences.evidence: With guards step 3 layout_brief: 'Build one route for a 5.9 x 6.27 m cell, then give each of six players their own copy in six separate cells arranged 2 x 3'. Before guards step 3 layout_brief: 'two long, gently bending lanes spanning the full 22 m court' and 'six separated spawn positions' — the math for 6 players on 2 lanes is not addressed.

differences.aspect: Consistency between steps: options → prototype → build plan
differences.with_rag: With guards maintains consistency: option 1 describes 8 checkpoints, 6 hazards, 300 seconds, cell-based layout; prototype plan uses 8 checkpoints, 6 hazards, 300 seconds, cell layout; build plan uses 8 checkpoints, 6 hazards, 300 seconds, cell layout.
differences.without_rag: Before guards maintains consistency: option 1 describes 9 checkpoints, hazards, 5 minutes, two lanes; prototype plan uses 9 checkpoints, hazards, 5 minutes, two lanes; build plan uses 9 checkpoints, hazards, 5 minutes, two lanes.
differences.evidence: Both designs carry forward the same core parameters (checkpoint count, hazard count, time limit, route structure) from options through prototype to build plan without contradiction.

differences.aspect: Spectator experience
differences.with_rag: With guards positions the final hazard (H6) and finish portal near the spectator side, with live leaderboard on the wall screen. Spectators see the final dodge and finish clearly.
differences.without_rag: Before guards positions the final two hazard groups, checkpoint 9, and finish portal near the long spectator side, with the wall leaderboard visible. Spectators see the climax bridge dodge and finish.
differences.evidence: Both designs place the climax and finish near spectators and use a wall-mounted leaderboard. With guards step 3: 'position H6 and the finish portal so they can see players' bodies'. Before guards step 3: 'Position the final two electrical hazard groups, checkpoint 9, and the finish portal near that long side'.

differences.aspect: Game feel: challenge and fellowship
differences.with_rag: With guards creates challenge through time pressure, hazards, and live leaderboard; fellowship through shared race experience and spectator cheering. The story involves restoring power to a neon city.
differences.without_rag: Before guards creates challenge through time pressure, hazards, and live leaderboard; fellowship through shared race experience and spectator cheering. The story involves delivering a power core to restore a neon city.
differences.evidence: Both designs use similar mechanics (checkpoints, hazards, time limit, leaderboard) and themes (neon city, power restoration) to achieve challenge and fellowship. Equivalent emotional targeting.

differences.aspect: Alternative options quality
differences.with_rag: With guards offers a sword-fighting option (acknowledged as deviating from the running brief) and a tactical board-game option (acknowledged as slower than running). Both are clearly framed as alternatives with trade-offs.
differences.without_rag: Before guards offers a tactical board-game option (acknowledged as changing from running to planning) and a sword-fighting option (acknowledged as farthest from the running brief). Both are clearly framed as alternatives with trade-offs.
differences.evidence: Both sessions provide three options with the first being the recommended running race and the other two being genre variations with explicit acknowledgment of deviation from the brief. Equivalent option diversity and honesty.

with_rag_weaknesses: Does not explicitly state 'no looking up while moving' as a safety constraint (Before guards does).
The cell-based approach, while safe, may feel less epic than using the full 22 m court length.
without_rag_weaknesses: Does not resolve how 6 players safely share two long lanes spanning the full 22 m court — the spatial plan is ambiguous and risks collision or interference.
Hazard placement is described by density zones rather than exact positions, making implementation less precise.
The risks section acknowledges the shared-space problem but the build plan does not solve it.
improvements: Before guards should specify how 6 players are physically separated when using two long lanes spanning the full 22 m court — the current plan risks player interference or collision.
Before guards should provide more granular hazard positions (like With guards's H1-H6 specification) rather than only describing density zones.
With guards could add the 'no looking up while moving' constraint that Before guards includes, to further improve safety.
Both designs could benefit from specifying exact cell/lane dimensions relative to the full court to verify fit.
